verdict.rationale: Letta documents adding memories from conversations: the /remember command commits lessons to MemFS, and dreaming subagents review recent conversations and update memory. Memory persists across sessions, since agents are resumed with their long-term memory. Semantic retrieval, however, is only an optional add-on: keyword, semantic or hybrid search requires installing the MemFS Search mod, and /search is documented only as searching messages, with no stated semantic mode. Missing for 10: built-in semantic search over memories, documentation of how the search mod works or how well it retrieves, and hands-on evidence of recall quality.

support.subject: As a developer, I can add memories from conversations and retrieve them later with semantic search, so context persists across sessions

citations.quote: The agent decides where the lesson belongs and commits the update to MemFS.
Dreaming uses background subagents to review recent conversations, consolidate useful lessons, and update memory without interrupting your active work.
For keyword search and optional semantic or hybrid search, install the [MemFS Search mod]
create an agent once, then resume it from anywhere. Each agent has its own identity and long-term memory
You can return to the same agent across sessions, computers, and interfaces instead of starting from scratch each time.
